nodes.title: Exclude exact rational order 25
nodes.summary: Prove that no rational point on an elliptic curve over Q has exact additive order 25. The checked Tate recurrence computes (n+2)P from index n and proves every secant denominator through 13P nonzero from exact order 25. Explicit square/cube normalized coordinates through 13P reduce x(13P)=x(12P) to the cuspidal factor b-c times one fixed 234-term polynomial of total degree 40. Checked Lécacheux modular units give five nonzero orbit coordinates, and all six cyclic relations needed to recover the invariant and force two selected units to be roots of Lehmer's quintic now hold for the actual Tate cross-ratios; the symmetric invariant is also recovered by a pole-free formula from two consecutive roots. A three-integral recovered invariant is impossible by the checked F₃ open-chart enumeration. Independently, explicit Tate normalization at 5P retains equal nonzero order-five parameters, and the five-isogeny route reaches one oriented five-division component, maps it to the explicit X₀(25) degeneracy curve, recovers a rational Hauptmodul without exceptional rational poles, and proves that n ↦ 5/n exchanges the two X₀(5) degeneracy values. Both actual degeneracy values are now identified with the same signed orbit Hauptmodul: the fifth-multiple Tate parameter is a rational fifth power k⁵ and the signed Hauptmodul is k - 1/k - 1. The residual exact-order case forces k to be a non-three-unit while -5/(k - 1/k - 1) is three-integral. Substitution into Lehmer's quintic gives one explicit integral two-variable cover P(k,x)=0, invariant under k ↦ -1/k, and the actual point supplies a noncuspidal rational solution x ≠ 0,1. The deck involution orients this solution as primitive integer coordinates k=m/n and x=u/v with 3 dividing m but not n; denominator clearing gives a checked homogeneous equation, whose reduction proves exactly one of u and v is divisible by 3. The pole-free Lehmer root transformation is now checked algebraically, agrees with the existing orbit, and cycles the five actual rational roots x₀→x₁→x₂→x₃→x₄→x₀. For the oriented scale v₃(k)=a>0, the exact 3-adic coefficient valuations and Newton slopes are checked directly, and the product and cubic Vieta identities sharpen the actual five-root valuation multiset to {3a,a,-a,-a,-2a}. The explicit deck-map valuation transitions and norm-one relation further force the cyclic order (3a,-a,a,-2a,-a), up to rotation. The two -a-valued roots additionally have three-integral difference from the negatively valued Lehmer parameter, identifying the diagonal infinity node in the plane model. Exact ratio valuations locate the remaining slopes as well, so all five branches are assigned to one of the three infinity charts. The checked degree-six homogenization factors at infinity as -N²X²(X-N)², proving that these charts target exactly the three nonzero projective directions and assigning every actual cyclic branch to one of them. Explicit strict transforms then resolve those directions into two, two, and one branches, giving all five points above infinity algebraically. Homogeneous rescaling now lifts every actual cyclic root to its strict-transform equation with exact local three-adic coordinate bounds. Exceptional-factor congruences sharpen this to the two root-zero residues, the two diagonal residues, and the unique smooth parameter-zero branch. The local deck map further separates the diagonal pair: successor slope a gives residue -2, while successor slope 3a gives residue -1. Together these results determine the exact cyclic order of all five resolved cusps, up to rotation. The cusp-order vector (3,-1,1,-2,-1) is now isolated as an explicit divisor-class interface; a checked integral row identity proves that its five cyclic relations annihilate every cusp difference by 71 and gives exact order 71 for distinct adjacent classes. Further checked row reductions express the other based differences as 6, 31, and 14 times the first, identify the full based cuspidal subgroup with that single cyclic span, compute its cardinality as 71, and construct an additive equivalence with Z/71Z. nodes.title: Cyclic subgroup quotients and classifying data
nodes.summary: The canonical commutative group scheme on the concrete projective Weierstrass cubic, its exact-torsion finite-flat cyclic subgroup, and its represented quotient now expose the kernel and base-change laws exercised by the X_0 and order-49 consumers. The ordinary D(x₁ - x₂) secant chart and D(B₁₂) product-neighbourhood chart carry actual over-base addition morphisms, with B₁₂ := y₁ + y₂ + a₁x₁ + a₃; their restricted projective morphisms agree on the exact intersection, and the second restricts to tangent doubling on the diagonal. Two denominator-cleared infinity-output charts extend those formulas across inverse pairs. All six pairwise restrictions of the four charts agree as actual scheme morphisms on their pullbacks, nonsingularity proves that the four principal opens cover the entire affine-pair presentation, and those charts are glued to an actual morphism from that affine-pair scheme into the concrete projective cubic. The full projective product is now covered by the four products of the genuine Y ≠ 0 and Z ≠ 0 cubic charts, and its standard-by-standard member is canonically identified with the affine-pair presentation and consumes the glued morphism. Every one of the four product members is now identified with the spectrum of the tensor product of its two chart coordinate rings; a K-algebra formula into that tensor product produces an automatically over-base scheme morphism, with both input projections checked as consumers. Each factor also has a normalized universal homogeneous point, and both embedded inputs are proved to satisfy the mapped cubic equation in every pair ring. For elliptic curves, every pair ring is now an integral domain; the raw homogeneous secant triple and both universal doubling triples satisfy the mapped cubic equation, and the secant output Z coordinate obeys the exact cubic cross-difference denominator identity. A normalized-point quotient-chart constructor turns the secant triple into honest over-base addition morphisms on both principal opens where its output Y or Z coordinate is invertible, for every projective-pair member. The same construction gives honest over-base first-input doubling morphisms on both doubling-output principal opens. A fraction-field argument using nonsingularity proves that these four principal opens jointly cover every pair member, and the two secant normalizations now agree as actual cubic-valued morphisms on their exact YZ overlap. The doubling morphisms agree with addition only on the diagonal; their unrestricted opens are therefore a nonvanishing certificate, not a four-open addition atlas. On the infinity-by-infinity chart, subtracting the two normalized cubic equations factors as `(z₁ - z₂) B∞ = (x₁ - x₂) A∞`; the principal neighborhood `D(B∞)` carries the regular slope `A∞ / B∞`. On the diagonal `B∞` is exactly the projective Z partial derivative, and an explicit evaluation map through the localization proves that `(O, O)` belongs to this neighborhood and that its slope is zero there. A denominator-free third-intersection calculation now turns that slope into homogeneous addition coordinates satisfying the mapped cubic without cancelling `x₁ - x₂` or the new homogeneous coordinate. Localizing at the output Y coordinate gives an actual open neighborhood of `(O, O)` and an over-base addition morphism into the concrete cubic; evaluation at `(O, O)` extends through both localizations. The raw secant triple is now proved to equal `(x₁ - x₂)³` times this regular triple on `D(B∞)`. On the exact principal overlap `D(B∞ · Ysec)`, both source restrictions are open immersions into the same pair chart and their normalized points and actual cubic-valued morphisms agree. Global projective addition, all commutative group laws, and the canonical coordinate-point addition comparison are now checked; the named order-49 consumer now derives the group object and point compatibility canonically, without supplied shadow inputs. The canonical exact-torsion finite-flat subgroup is now constructed from every exact-order coordinate point, has checked constant geometric order, and recovers the original rational Γ₀ datum; the order-49 consumers no longer accept an arbitrary group-scheme interface. The represented cyclic quotient is now bundled as an abelian variety with a finite étale fppf projection, exact canonical kernel, rational-point boundary exactness, and arbitrary-base-change kernel exactness; the order-49 presentation is its named downstream consumer. Separately, an actual finite free-translation quotient of a supplied commutative group scheme transfers geometric integrality, local finite type, flatness, separatedness, properness, and smoothness under the theorem-specific source hypotheses, together with an affine diagonal, finite section action, stable affine atlas, and scheme-theoretic freeness; the local-finite-type, proper, and smooth results use an affine noetherian base. The field-level abelian-variety quotient is its named consumer. The generic substrate does not instantiate those objects by itself; the canonical projective-cubic layer now supplies the Weierstrass source, exact-torsion subgroup, represented cyclic quotient, and its arbitrary-base-change kernel law. At the point-group level, no equality between quotient-scheme K-points and the quotient of K-points is asserted without controlling the H1 connecting class.

external_reuse.status: strong substrate with central open gates
external_reuse.summary: AINTLIB supplies elliptic torsion subgroup schemes, multiplication kernels, a finite-action quotient scheme and universal property, field-level pairing work, and finite-flat examples; this project equips the actual finite free-translation quotient with a commutative group law and proves its generic geometry over affine noetherian bases.
external_reuse.boundary: The construction still starts from a supplied source commutative group scheme with affine diagonal, a finite section action, stable affine atlas, and scheme-theoretic freeness proof, plus the source geometric hypotheses required by each transfer theorem. Local finite type uses a locally-finite-type source over an affine noetherian base; properness uses a proper source over that base; smoothness separately uses a flat, locally-finite-type, geometrically reduced source over that base. It does not construct the canonical Weierstrass group scheme, exact-torsion subgroup, desired cyclic quotient instance, arbitrary-base-change kernel law, dual isogeny, or global scheme-valued Weil pairing, so it does not discharge this node by itself.

nodes.title: Neron models for the Eisenstein quotient
nodes.summary: The canonical supplied Neron-model interface, mapping property, and section-extension equivalences compile. Separately, properness of an actual commutative group model over a valuation ring gives a terminal-point equivalence between its integral points and the points of an identified generic fibre. Over an affine noetherian base, the generic finite-translation quotient layer proves properness from a proper source and proves smoothness separately from a flat, locally-finite-type, geometrically reduced source; both results retain the supplied affine diagonal, section action, invariant affine atlas, and freeness proof. It neither identifies the arithmetic Eisenstein quotient or its generic fibre nor proves the Neron mapping property. Construct the abelian-variety Neron substrate at the required arithmetic DVRs, then realize the actual optimal Eisenstein quotient and its cusp-normalized map in that model for the rank-zero and collision consumers. The marked source point's exact-order reduction at 5 is already checked independently and does not require a source elliptic Neron model.

nodes.title: Identity components and toric modular fibres
nodes.summary: Define genuine Neron identity components and component groups and prove completely toric reduction at the modular level for the Eisenstein rank-zero criterion. The canonical nonsingular-reduction subgroup, its additive map, exact formal kernel, finite cuspidal classification, unit-change transport, and the full marked tangent--secant/weighted-depth calculation already compile at five and eleven. That pointwise calculation now forces a4 in m⁴ and a6 in m⁶ and contradicts minimality, so the local prime and order-35 arithmetic endpoints no longer depend on component geometry. The open node is the represented identity-component/component-quotient and toric modular input consumed by rank zero; no Kodaira or full component-cardinality result is inferred from the checked chart algebra.

nodes.title: The X_0(N) moduli point attached to rational prime torsion
nodes.summary: Construct the split rational cyclic subgroup generated by a torsion point, its intrinsic divisor subgroups and degeneracy maps, and quotient raw Weierstrass data by checked admissible variable changes. For coprime divisor levels whose product is N, a checked Bezout argument proves that the two intrinsic divisor subgroups generate the original carrier; the order-five/order-seven level-35 reconstruction is its concrete consumer. The canonical projective group scheme, exact-torsion finite-flat subgroup, and represented cyclic quotient are now available. A split geometric Gamma-zero object bundles the proper geometrically integral relative curve and its actual finite-flat cyclic subgroup. The arbitrary-base layer constructs the constant cyclic group over every scheme, fppf-locally constant cyclic subgroup data, its global order theorem, and a relative Gamma-zero family. Pullback along any base morphism transports the actual fppf cover through the pullback square and canonical iterated-base-change comparisons. Subgroup-preserving isomorphisms now quotient these relative families, pullback descends to the quotient, and canonical identity and composition isomorphisms prove the laws of an actual contravariant type-valued moduli functor. The intrinsic field quotient maps into it without choosing representatives, and exact order-49 torsion reaches both its Q-value and every reindexed value. A representing open X_0(N), universal-family comparison, and generalized bad-characteristic cyclicity remain absent, so the selected package and node stay blocked. The represented polynomial cusp chart and its local sections do not construct the missing Gamma_0 classifier.

theorem cyclotomic_locallyPrimaryPseudoUnitKummerReciprocityPrinciple
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (_hp : 5 ≤ p) :
    LocallyPrimaryPseudoUnitKummerReciprocityPrinciple.{u} p := sorry
challenge.informal: For every prime p at least 5 and every inverse-cyclotomic degree-p Kummer extension of Q(zeta_p), if the canonical radicand has p-divisible finite divisor and is a p-th power in the completion at the unique prime above p, its finite Kummer/Frobenius product is one on every nonzero integral principal denominator outside that prime. The destination already proves both radicand hypotheses for an everywhere-unramified extension, compares Kummer and Artin coordinates, clears fractional denominators, and removes the cyclotomic-prime factor.
challenge.recommended_route: Prove one-sided Kummer reciprocity for a locally-primary pseudo-unit, first for integral denominators coprime to the radicand and p; then extend across the finite bad set. The Kummer/Frobenius comparison and prime-complement denominator clearing are already checked in the destination. Alternatively prove the same integral vanishing via the conductor-one cyclic Artin reciprocity theorem.
